user.title: Create a light compositor
user.description: Select a light or a compatible Home Assistant or Zigbee2MQTT light group. Native Zigbee2MQTT groups require discovered membership and compatible MQTT members on the same bridge. The base is fixed after setup. Leave Name empty to use the base's name. Setup starts with Apply off. Use the generated Main control light in ordinary lighting automations instead of the base; it remembers everyday power, brightness and color beneath the masks. Use separate masks for notifications. Do not also control the base or group members from other automations.

zone.description: {count} zones added. Each zone needs a disjoint Zigbee2MQTT group on the same bridge with identical capabilities. All members of each zone must have the same known power state during enrollment. Zone topology is fixed after setup.

aggregate.title: Review zones and optional aggregate
aggregate.description: Zones: {zones}. The optional native aggregate must contain exactly the union of these zones. It is used only when all zones are available and need identical commands; otherwise native zone groups are used. Whole Main is On if any ordinary zone is On; its toggle then requests all Off. Mixed color and brightness are not averaged. Masks apply to every zone. Unknown/unavailable members block only their zone; healthy zones continue with overall degraded status. Unsafe topology still blocks the compositor. Setup starts with Apply Off.

base.title: Name and main control
base.description: Fixed base: {output}. Name labels this setup and its devices; it does not change entity IDs or lighting behavior. Use Main control for ordinary lighting automations, not the base. Main control remembers everyday power, brightness and color; masks temporarily override selected channels. Main control Off requests darkness, while mask Off releases that mask. Power-controlling masks can override Main control's power. To use a different base, create a new Light Masks entry.

data_description.name: Display name of this compositor; the physical output cannot be replaced here.

add_mask.title: Add mask
add_mask.description: Choose which parts of the base light this mask may override. Turning the mask On activates those contributions; turning it Off removes them and reveals Main control or other active masks. Device-page permission indicators show these settings, not which mask currently wins.

data.restore: Restore activation after restart or manual reload
data.duration: Maximum duration in seconds (0 disables expiry)

data_description.name: Display name of this independent mask device.
data_description.restore: Restore activation after restart or manual reload if its lease has not expired. Values are always retained.
data_description.power: Unchecked: this mask cannot turn the base on or off; it only changes selected brightness/color when lighting is on. Checked: while active, it requests On at its priority, even if Main control is Off, unless a higher-priority power mask wins. Turning this mask Off releases its request; the base stays On if another request requires it. Apply and safety protections still apply.
data_description.brightness: Allow this mask's stored brightness to override lower-priority brightness. Unchecked: brightness remains local to this mask, even if Home Assistant's color-light card displays a brightness slider.
data_description.appearance: Allow this mask's stored RGB color or color temperature to override lower-priority color. Independent of Control brightness; only modes supported by the base are available.
data_description.priority: 100 overrides 10. The highest active priority wins each enabled channel separately. Priorities must be unique for this base.
data_description.duration: Automatically release the mask after this many seconds. Each turn_on action starts a fresh timer, including color/brightness updates while already On. 0 means no automatic release.

data_description.mask: Existing mask whose permissions or lease settings you want to edit.

mask.title: Edit mask
mask.description: Saving keeps this mask's current On/Off state and stored values. Permission and priority changes take effect immediately. Device-page permission indicators update to match these settings.

storage.title: Light Masks could not save intent
storage.description: A storage operation for {output} failed. Output writes are blocked. Check disk space, permissions and the log. After fixing storage, reload or use the Retry after fixing a fault action. Resubmit rejected commands.

delivery.title: Light Masks output did not converge
delivery.description: {output} did not converge, or external controls repeatedly overrode it. Check connectivity and stop competing writers. Delivery attempts are bounded; Sync, a new command, or actual output recovery can retry. Unsafe topology and storage faults stay blocked.

endpoint.title: Light Masks output is no longer safe to control
endpoint.description: {output} has invalid feedback, unsupported capabilities, conflicting ownership, or changed membership. Inspect the log and configuration before using Retry after fixing a fault. Restore the original topology or recreate the entry for a different output.

explain.name: Explain
explain.description: Return stored intents, desired and observed state, and channel ownership. User calls require administrator permission.

resume.name: Retry after fixing a fault
resume.description: Compatibility action: revalidate topology and storage, then retry. Normal external-change, reconnect and restart recovery is automatic. Apply must be enabled. Administrator permission is required.

sync.name: Sync
sync.description: Retry the current calculated result without clearing storage or unsafe-topology faults. User calls require administrator permission.

clear_fields.name: Clear mask fields
clear_fields.description: Unset selected stored contributions without releasing mask activation. User calls require administrator permission.
